title: Billing a Circle Dues Period and Applying What the Member Pays
content:
## Billing a period of Circle dues

Dues on a Northbeam Circle Membership are billed for a whole billing period at the dues figure of the
tier recorded on the membership on the first day of that period, annually or monthly according to the
billing frequency the membership is held on. The amount billed for a full annual period is the annual
dues figure of that tier. The dues standing against a membership are the dues and fees billed and not yet
settled: a charge raises them and money received reduces them.

Dues are billed, and payments applied, only while the membership record stands as an application
received, active or in grace. The standing recorded on the membership named is read before the charge or
the payment is taken, from the record rather than from the caller's account of it.

## The other charges this policy raises

The enrolment fee, where the tier charges one, is billed once on the enrolment day and is never refunded
on cancellation.

## How money received is applied

A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid billing period first, and any remainder to the next. A payment
larger than everything outstanding leaves the surplus as unapplied credit on the membership rather than
being returned.

## Settlement methods and invoice terms

Business tiers may settle dues on invoice, and an invoice is treated as unpaid only after its terms have
run; consumer tiers settle on the card on file or from store credit. The methods open to a tier and the
days an invoice may run are the ones recorded for that tier.

## Dues for a period already used

Dues already billed for a period the customer has used are owed in full even if the membership later
lapses or is cancelled.

## Worked application of a payment

Take a membership on Circle Total Household Annual carrying two unpaid monthly periods, 21.99 for the older
period and 21.99 for the newer, and a payment of 30.00. The older period takes 21.99 and the remainder of
8.01 goes against the newer period, which is then short by 13.98. Had the payment been 50.00, both periods
would be met and the surplus of 6.02 would stand as unapplied credit on the membership rather than being paid
back.
